evidence.supports: Confirms the road-use moratorium, its July 2025 origin, its June 1, 2026 extension vote, and its scope (wind and solar construction traffic on county-maintained roads).
evidence.quote: The McIntosh County Board of County Commissioners voted Monday, June 1, to extend its moratorium on the use of county-maintained roads for the transport and delivery of equipment and materials associated with the construction of wind turbines, solar panels, and related infrastructure. The county's road moratorium was first enacted in July 2025 after commissioners raised concerns about the potential impact of large-scale renewable energy projects on local infrastructure.

evidence.supports: Independently describes McIntosh County as adopting a one-year moratorium on new wind projects in April 2026, tied to Badger Wind Farm coming online and a second proposed Orsted project.
evidence.quote: Nevertheless, in April — a few months after Badger Wind Farm went online — McIntosh County adopted a one-year moratorium on new wind projects, citing concerns about how another Orsted project, proposed for the south part of the county, would impact nonparticipant property owners.

decisions.notes: The documented, primary-adjacent instrument -- a road-use moratorium on county-maintained roads for wind/solar construction traffic, first enacted July 2025 and extended by commissioner vote June 1, 2026 -- is well sourced with direct quotes from a specialized local outlet (McIntosh Democrat) and functions as a genuine, if narrowly mechanised, construction pause (without road access, construction cannot proceed), satisfying criterion (a). I additionally checked the packet's flagged discrepancy against a national feature-piece claim that McIntosh County 'adopted a one-year moratorium on new wind projects' in April 2026 (Canary Media, Mother Jones, and now also CRBC News -- three outlets, all without a cited ordinance/resolution number, and all describing the action only as 'shortly after Badger [Wind Farm] came online' in January 2026). Given the original ordinance was itself a 12-month term running from its July 2025 enactment, and given the specificity and named-commissioner detail of the McIntosh Democrat's road-moratorium reporting versus the vaguer general-audience framing in the national pieces, I judge these are very likely the same underlying action described two different ways (with the national outlets approximating the date), rather than two distinct instruments. Kept as-is; flagging for the coordinator in case a future pass turns up the actual county resolution.

evidence.supports: Confirms the 2026-09-22 unanimous board vote to hold a public hearing on a proposed two-year moratorium covering solar, wind, data centers, battery storage, transmission lines, and gas generation, and the related legal-review motion.
evidence.quote: Burchill made a motion, which passed unanimously, to hold a public hearing that would serve as a formal opportunity for people to comment on whether they think a moratorium is appropriate. The language he used in his motion ... was for a two-year zoning moratorium for all industrial-scale development including solar, wind, data centers, battery storage systems, electric transmission lines and gas-fired electrical generation facilities “in order to update its zoning ordinances to further protect the township and its residents.”

decisions.notes: Verified against InForum's Sept. 22-23, 2026 report: the board voted unanimously only to hold a public hearing on a proposed two-year moratorium; no hearing date set, no adoption. 'pending' correct.
